In June, the UN-backed IPC reported 5.1 million people facing severe hunger, as farmers struggle to harvest amid war and a recent wave of drought.

Vernet's Mamelouk: The East in French Eyes

Portrait of a "Mamelouk" (1810, oil on canvas) is an early work by Horace Vernet (Paris 1789–1863 Paris), painted when the artist was around twenty. The Mamluks were an elite cavalry caste that dominated Egypt for centuries; after Napoleon's Egyptian campaign began in 1798, a Mamluk squadron served in his Imperial Guard, and the figure of the Mamluk entered French visual culture.

The quotation marks in the title invite caution: the painting tells us as much about French fascination with the 'Orient' as about the sitter himself. Read with scholarly nuance, it shows how costume, military glamour and imagination shaped European images of the Islamic world in the Napoleonic era.

Vernet, son of the painter Carle Vernet, later travelled with French forces in Algeria and became one of the best-known painters of large battle scenes in nineteenth-century France. The work is in the collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

Source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art

Türkiye's parliament has ratified the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, passing it by 279 votes to 119, with 398 of the chamber's 592 members voting. The pact was signed at a trilateral summit in Mecca on 7 August 2026 and contains 16 articles. Its Article 2 obliges members to assist any party subjected to armed attack, a clause that mirrors Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty. It binds members for 10 years and allows new members with unanimous approval; Syria has expressed interest.

The ratification comes as Riyadh faces escalating attacks from Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis. AK Party MP Ziya Altunyaldiz said the agreement targets no third country, while CHP MP Mehmet Guzelmansur called for clear rules so it does not contradict Türkiye's other international obligations. Critics have raised questions of a conflict of interest with NATO commitments, which Turkish officials dismiss.

Defence Minister Yasar Guler has said Türkiye does not foresee conflict with the Houthis and that its support would aim to strengthen deterrence. Any troop deployment would require a separate parliamentary mandate.

On Friday, the office of Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani said he spoke by phone with US President Donald Trump about de-escalation and a comprehensive agreement, stressing freedom of navigation and the security of energy supplies. Qatar, alongside Pakistan, has been mediating since the war began with US and Israeli attacks on Iran in late February; Qatari officials have shuttled between Doha and Tehran, including over the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

Ali Baqeri, deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said Tehran will not rely on US commitments on paper, arguing Washington derailed four rounds of talks over 18 months, and that practical American actions must come first.
